svg.title: Urinary tract obstruction decision chart: an upper-tract block from a stone (renal colic) sorted by fever and stone size into an infected obstructing stone needing urgent drainage, a small stone likely to pass, or a large or failing stone needing lithotripsy or nephrolithotomy; a lower-tract block (urinary retention at the bladder outlet) relieved by catheter with watch for post-obstructive diuresis; plus how to prevent the next stone

svg.text: Urine flow BLOCKED: WHERE, and how BAD?

svg.text: hydronephrosis (dilated pelvis + calyces) on ultrasound or computed tomography (CT) · it can occur WITHOUT a block (reflux)

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: worse if: COMPLETE · BOTH sides · INFECTED (speeds nephron loss) · > 6 WEEKS complete = function lost for good

svg.text: UPPER tract, one side: RENAL COLIC from a stone

svg.text: severe one-sided flank pain in WAVES → groin, scrotum or labia · hematuria · vomiting

svg.text: 1 · CT (most sensitive) · ultrasound sees every stone · plain x-ray MISSES uric acid stones

svg.text: also think: aortic aneurysm, pyelonephritis, a mass, musculoskeletal
